subject.title: Question: Publisher verification path for active code plugin contributors?

question: Should ClawHub offer a public Verified or vetted-community path for third-party code-plugin publishers, and if so should it be publisher-scoped, package-scoped, or release-scoped?
rationale: This trust signal would influence install decisions for executable community plugins, so automation cannot safely choose the policy, criteria, authority, revocation model, or wording.

options.title: Use the RFC as canonical policy work
options.body: Keep this issue linked as author-specific context and make https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2272 the place where maintainers decide the trust model before implementation.

options.title: Document no community Verified path
options.body: State that Official remains staff-controlled and community packages rely on source linkage, scan status, and release trust summaries for now.

options.title: Pilot a vetted-community cohort
options.body: Define a small security-reviewed cohort with explicit criteria, evidence, expiry, and revocation before adding schema, API, UI, or docs surface.

recommendation.title: Use the RFC as canonical policy work
recommendation.body: Keep this issue linked as author-specific context and make https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2272 the place where maintainers decide the trust model before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is the strongest current-main history signal for Official publisher policy, trusted publishing, package channel schema, and scanner/trust surfaces.
